scores.claim_text: Teal selected as winner of U.S. Army SRR Program of Record (Nov 2024); FY2025 revenue growth attributed primarily to scaling drone deliveries under SRR program.
supports: usaspending.query_dod_contracts: Teal Drones 27 awards, $2.17M total; largest single award $750K (FA700025P0127 for 74 Teal 2 drones to USAFA/A3); no award description mentions 'Short Range Reconnaissance' or 'Program of Record'
usaspending.query_recipient_contracts: Red Cat Holdings 18 awards $3.79M total across DoD ($pieces), DHS, USDA, VA — bulk to non-DoD agencies
Award IDs are predominantly Air Force base-level FA-series purchase orders ranging $15K-$750K, plus Army National Guard small buys — not Program-of-Record IDIQ ceilings
scores.M_check: usaspending.gov DoD obligations to all RCAT recipient name variants (Red Cat, Teal Drones, FlightWave, Red Cat Holdings, Skypersonic)
scores.interpretation: RCAT claims FY2025 $40.7M revenue with ~73% from US Government (~$29.7M), primarily driven by SRR Program of Record scaling. USAspending shows only ~$4.9M of DoD obligations across ALL RCAT subsidiaries (Teal, FlightWave, Red Cat) and ~$7.0M including non-DoD federal — a ~4-6x gap vs. claimed government revenue. Per Heuristic 9 (DoD-CONTRACT-SPECIFIC): absence of SRR-named obligations for a company claiming an SRR Program of Record win is a hard contradiction. Could be explained by: (1) deliveries flowing through DLA/intermediaries not captured by recipient search; (2) IDIQ task orders not yet obligated; (3) sales to Defense Innovation Unit/Blue UAS Marketplace channel; or (4) genuine overstatement. Caveat: 2.5 page-result limit on top_awards may miss aggregation tail. The 27-award Teal total $2.17M is real, but $4.9M aggregate << $29.7M claimed. Severity: SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY rather than RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE because some DoD presence exists and the program selection date (Nov 2024) is recent enough that ramp-up could lag obligation visibility — but the gap is large and SRR program-of-record awards should appear by FY2025 close.

scores.claim_text: FY2025: ~73% of $40.7M revenue from US Government (~$29.7M).
supports: Sum of USAspending-traceable federal obligations to all RCAT subsidiaries: ~$7M lifetime, of which ~$4.9M is DoD
Even if all $4.9M DoD obligations to Teal+FlightWave+Red Cat had occurred in FY2025 alone (they did not — they accumulate 2020-2026), the figure is ~16% of claimed FY2025 US-Govt revenue
Concentration disclosure shows one customer = 73% of FY2025 revenue (Customer A: 88% of receivables) — consistent with single-program reliance
scores.M_check: USAspending sum across recipient name variants; cross-check against 73% US-Govt revenue concentration disclosure
scores.interpretation: Either claimed revenue substantially overstates real federal demand, OR USAspending recipient-name search materially undercounts via (a) prime-sub flow-throughs where RCAT is a subcontractor not the named recipient (NDAA/Blue UAS purchases via large primes); (b) sales through DIU's Blue UAS Marketplace where final recipient may be a procurement office aggregator; (c) Foreign Military Sales not in USAspending. Customer A at 73% revenue is consistent with a single Program-of-Record buyer — but that buyer's purchases should appear as obligations. This is the same divergence pattern as C1 — sized at fiscal-year resolution. Severity: SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY.

scores.claim_text: Teal 2 is Blue UAS Certified by DoD.
supports: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts: at least one Teal Drones award explicitly references 'DEFENSE INNOVATION UNIT APPROVED BLUE SUAS UNITS' (FA820124F0312, $56,223), confirming DIU/Blue UAS pathway
scores.M_check: USAspending search for DIU / Blue UAS award descriptions to Teal Drones
scores.interpretation: Direct USAspending corroboration of Blue UAS / DIU pathway. The Blue UAS certification claim is independently verified by a DIU-funded purchase order. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Partnership/development roadmap with AeroVironment (AVAV) — FANG FPV as P550 payload (marsupial config).
supports: edgar_fts AVAV CIK=0001368622: 3 hits for 'Red Cat' — all in DEF 14A filings (2023, 2024, 2025), almost certainly executive-compensation peer-group disclosure rather than substantive partnership
edgar_fts AVAV: 0 hits for 'FANG' and 0 hits for 'Teal Drones'
Red Cat's own filings mention AeroVironment 10 times — but partnership corroboration requires reciprocal disclosure
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext on AVAV (CIK=0001368622) for distinctive product/co name terms
scores.interpretation: AVAV's disclosure does not corroborate the partnership in any substantive form (no product names, no operational language; only DEF 14A appearances consistent with comp-peer listing). However, per Heuristic 4 (Investment vs operating partnerships) and Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold), a 'development roadmap' / early integration partnership announced in 8-Ks is NOT material enough to trigger AVAV's own 10-K disclosure obligations. The partnership is plausibly real and announced bilaterally but has no commercial obligations yet. UNVERIFIABLE rather than SEVERE because the materiality threshold for AVAV is not met.

scores.claim_text: Successfully completed flight testing of Black Widow drone with Palantir VNav software in GPS-denied conditions.
supports: edgar_fts Palantir CIK=0001321655: 0 hits for 'Red Cat', 0 hits for 'Black Widow', 0 hits for 'VNav' — Palantir does not disclose this in any SEC filing
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext on PLTR (CIK=0001321655) for Red Cat / Black Widow / VNav
scores.interpretation: Palantir's filings contain no mention of Red Cat, Black Widow, or VNav. Per Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold): for Palantir ($100B+ company), a single drone-vendor flight test would not meet materiality threshold for 10-K disclosure. The claim is a 'successful flight test' — not a contract, revenue, or commitment — and is independently a low-bar marketing claim. UNVERIFIABLE rather than SEVERE because the materiality bar at PLTR is high and the claim itself is operational not financial.

scores.claim_text: Operates manufacturing facilities in Salt Lake UT (37K sq ft), Valdosta GA (155K sq ft), Torrance CA (51K sq ft), Carson CA (14K sq ft).
supports: epa_frs.query_facilities: 'Teal' hits in GA/CA are all unrelated subdivisions/streets (Teal Lake, Teal Ranch, etc.) — no RCAT-affiliated facility found
Per Heuristic 1 (EPA FRS scope): drone assembly is not EPA-regulated process; absence from FRS is expected and not a contradiction
Lease schedule in Item 2 Properties is granular with addresses, monthly rents ($46K-$66K range), and expiration dates — internal consistency is high
scores.M_check: EPA FRS facility search by 'Teal' / 'Red Cat' / 'FlightWave' in UT, GA, CA
scores.interpretation: EPA FRS is the wrong M-source for drone-assembly facilities (Heuristic 1). The lease schedule is detailed enough to be internally falsifiable (monthly rents map roughly to claimed sq ft at credible $/sqft rates: 155K sq ft in Valdosta @ $48,550/mo = ~$3.75/sqft annual, plausible for rural GA industrial). PASS.

scores.claim_text: FlightWave (acquired Sept 2024) has existing relationships with several U.S. government agencies including classification as approved vendors — basis for $8.7M of goodwill.
supports: usaspending.query_dod_contracts: FlightWave 8 awards totaling $2.30M — confirms FlightWave does have DoD contracts
Total FlightWave obligations ($2.3M) is modest relative to $14M purchase price and $8.7M ascribed goodwill
Acquisition was Sept 2024; some obligations may post-date acquisition
scores.M_check: usaspending DoD obligations to FlightWave (recipient substring)
scores.interpretation: FlightWave's DoD presence is real but modest ($2.3M lifetime). Ascribing $8.7M of goodwill to 'approved vendor' relationships with 'several US government agencies' is a soft claim — the actually-traceable federal contracting footprint is small. Not a hard contradiction (federal relationship exists), but ratio of goodwill to demonstrable revenue history is high. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY.
